introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - Ordinary Level Examination. Logic (0590), Paper 2, June 2023. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Answer FIVE questions, taking ALL the THREE Questions from Section A and ANY TWO from Section B. ONLY THE FIRST FIVE QUESTIONS ANSWERED WILL BE MARKED.

All the questions carry 20 marks. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

In solving, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage.
incertitudes: Q6(a)(i) : « Medical doctors such as ... Diviners » : totum divisum = medical doctors, membra dividentia = les quatre spécialités citées ; la division est fautive (un devin n'est pas médecin), signalé dans le corrigé. Q6(a)(ii) : « this is the woman who deceived me and took my money » classé définition ostensive (démonstrative) avec description ; le manuel du programme peut la nommer autrement (définition par description / par exemple) : à confirmer.

Q6(c)(i) : « E and I given that O is false » : O faux donc A vrai (contradictoire), E faux (contraire), I vrai (subalterne, import existentiel) ; la conjonction est fausse même sans import existentiel (E faux).

Q6(d)(i) : le sujet appelle « Dilemma » un argument dont la majeure a un antécédent conjonctif (A et B) ; ce n'est pas rigoureusement un dilemme valide (le calcul montre l'invalidité). Réponse donnée : dilemme constructif simple (forme visée), avec la réserve. Q6(d)(ii) : « Dangote... Nigerians » : généralisation hâtive (forme de composition) ; si le manuel n'accepte que l'un des deux noms, les deux sont cités.

Aucun corrigé officiel ; les corrigés sont des réponses modèles de manuel de logique traditionnelle (définitions, règles de distribution, carré des oppositions avec import existentiel, ordres de l'enthymème : 1er = majeure supprimée, 2e = mineure supprimée, 3e = conclusion supprimée). Les tables de vérité, la validité des syllogismes (AOO-2, EOO-1, EIO-4) et du dilemme sont recalculées avec Python. À faire relire par un enseignant de logique : les définitions varient d'un manuel à l'autre.

Règle de choix : la page de garde dit « Answer FIVE questions, taking ALL the THREE Questions from Section A and ANY TWO from Section B ; only the first five questions answered will be marked ». Section A (questions 1 à 3) : toutes obligatoires, donc aucune règle ; Section B (questions 4 à 6) : `parmi 2 sur 3`. La règle « les cinq premières réponses seules sont corrigées » est recopiée dans `introduction_markdown`.
Points : chaque question est imprimée « 20 marks » ; chaque sous-question (a) à (e) vaut 4 points (« 2 x 2 marks », sauf Q2(a) imprimée « 4 x 1 marks »). 5 x 4 = 20 : aucun écart de somme.

Sujet scanné de 8 pages avec filigrane gcerevision.com / KAWLO, sans incidence sur la lecture ; aucune figure. Page de garde vérifiée : ORDINARY LEVEL EXAMINATION, Logic, code 0590, Paper 2, JUNE 2023, deux heures et demie.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) (i) In the expression, *Medical doctors such as Gynecologists, Pediatricians, Dermatologists and Diviners.* Identify the Totum Divisum and Membra Dividentia.

(ii) Identify the following Definitions: *this is the woman who deceived me and took my money.* (2 x 2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** The **totum divisum** is the whole that is divided: **"medical doctors"**. The **membra dividentia** are the parts or members into which it is divided: **Gynecologists, Pediatricians, Dermatologists and Diviners**. (Remark: "Diviners" are not medical doctors, so the division breaks the rule that each member must be a part of the whole; the question only asks to identify the two elements.)

**(ii)** The speaker points to an individual ("this is the woman") and describes her by what she did: it is an **ostensive (demonstrative) definition**, defining by pointing out the individual in the context, completed by a description of that individual. It does not define a class by genus and difference; it identifies a particular person.
themes: O Level Logic - definition and division

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) (i) Construct a Disjunctive Proposition with the same Subject and different Predicates using the Term *Miriam, spinster* and *Married woman.*

(ii) Translate the Proposition in b(i) above into a Hypothetical proposition. (2 x 2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** The subject is "Miriam" and the two predicates are "a spinster" and "a married woman":

**Miriam is either a spinster or a married woman.**

**(ii)** A disjunctive proposition "Either A or B" is turned into a hypothetical proposition by saying that if one alternative is false the other is true:

**If Miriam is not a spinster, then she is a married woman.** (Equivalent: If Miriam is not a married woman, then she is a spinster.)
themes: O Level Logic - propositions and their types

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) (i) What is the Truth-value of "E and I" given that "O" is false?

(ii) Obvert *All students are learners.* (2 x 2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** Use the square of opposition. If **O is false**, then its contradictory **A is true** (contradictories always have opposite truth-values). Since A is true:
- **E is false** (A and E are contraries: they cannot both be true);
- **I is true** (I is the subaltern of A, so it follows from a true A).

"E and I" is a conjunction whose first conjunct is false and whose second conjunct is true, so $F \cdot T = F$.

**The truth-value of "E and I" is false.** (E is false, so the conjunction is false whatever the value of I.)

**(ii) Obversion.** Keep the subject and the quantity, change the quality and replace the predicate by its contradictory:

**No students are non-learners.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(d) (i) Identify the form of this Dilemma:

*If the rains come early, and farmers plant in time then the harvest will be good.*

*Either the rains come early or farmers plant in time.*

*Therefore, the harvest will be good.*

(ii) Which Fallacy does this Argument commit?

*Dangote is very rich.*

*He is a Nigerian.*

*Therefore, all Nigerians are very rich.* (2 x 2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** The argument has a conditional major premise, a disjunctive minor premise with two alternatives, and one single conclusion that is the common consequent of both alternatives. It is the pattern of a **simple constructive dilemma**: If A then C; if B then C; either A or B; therefore C. The conclusion is the **same** consequent ("the harvest will be good") whichever alternative is chosen.

Strict check: as printed, the major premise has a **conjunctive antecedent** ($(A \cdot B) \supset C$), not two separate conditionals, and a truth-table check shows that from $(A \cdot B) \supset C$ and $A \vee B$ the conclusion $C$ does not follow (take $A$ true, $B$ false, $C$ false). So the printed argument is an **imperfect simple constructive dilemma** (it is invalid as worded); the form intended by the examiner is the simple constructive dilemma.

**(ii)** The argument concludes about **all** Nigerians from the wealth of **one** Nigerian: it is the fallacy of **hasty generalisation** (sweeping conclusion drawn from a single, unrepresentative case), a form of the **fallacy of composition** (what is true of one part is attributed to the whole class).

(e) (i) Determine the truth-value of $(\sim p \vee \sim q) \supset q$ when both p and q are False

(ii) Using the variables P as *parents pay fees*; A as *students attend classes regularly* and S as *success will be guaranteed*, express this function into ordinary language: $(\sim P \cdot \sim A) \supset \sim S$ (2 x 2 marks)
themes: O Level Logic - symbolic logic basics
